source_parts.text: Annotation quality is examined through a structured review of disagreements, ambiguous question wording, and omitted source qualifications. The most consequential errors arise when a passage is relevant to the topic but supports a different version or condition. This concern links the rubric to mapping a near-synonym to a semantically adjacent but wrong concept. Investigators ask whether the output retained the decisive concept definition, whether it attributed the result to the correct source release, and whether it overstated what the evidence could establish. These checks are not additional favorable outcomes that may replace the prespecified primary endpoint. They explain the interpretation of Recall@5 and identify threats to validity. The missing measurement of downstream clinical utility remains missing after this exercise, since checking source support does not automatically measure every downstream outcome.

source_parts.text: Efficiency claims require a joint description of resources, performance, and workload. For BioGloss-Sim, the workload consists of 1880 declared questions against 14200 frozen records, with five retrieved abstracts supplied to the downstream stage. Those conditions should accompany any attempt to compare resource figures. A system serving a different language mix, a larger collection, or a more demanding evidence policy could have a different resource profile even if its score were similar. We report the observed accounting status and leave the unobserved components unresolved. This restraint is especially important in a synthetic benchmark: plausible numerical detail should never be mistaken for a measurement of an actual service. All resource values in this manuscript are fictional controlled facts for evaluating source-grounded review behavior.

source_parts.text: The motivating failure is mapping a near-synonym to a semantically adjacent but wrong concept. In this setting a superficially relevant passage can contain the correct words while referring to an incompatible object, version, or condition. The intervention therefore uses explicit negative concept constraints as a constraint on evidence selection. The constraint is intended to alter the available support, not to rewrite the underlying source statements. We separate the proposition that a candidate was retrieved from the stronger proposition that an answer is justified. This distinction matters for Recall@5, whose operational definition addresses only the outcome specified in this paper. We do not substitute a favorable result on that outcome for measurements of every downstream property. In particular, downstream clinical utility was not measured, so conclusions about that property remain outside the observed evidence.

source_parts.text: The protocol requires the two conditions to keep the same output policy and the same definition of a supported answer. A pipeline is not permitted to manufacture a source statement merely because it retrieves a more convenient record. The source text remains authoritative when it contradicts the generated answer. Investigators inspect examples containing a nearby concept definition, since a short excerpt can appear persuasive after the limiting sentence is removed. These inspections inform the error taxonomy, but they do not replace the full scoring set. A collection of favorable examples would not estimate Recall@5. Conversely, a negative example can reveal a real failure mode without showing how common that failure is. We preserve both types of evidence and state which conclusions depend on aggregate scoring rather than on qualitative inspection.

source_parts.text: Evidence assembly preserves the smallest complete context that can support or refute an answer. In particular, a quantitative value must remain connected to its unit, population, and relevant qualification. Where a table contains the relevant value, its caption and notes accompany the selected cells. A nearby concept definition is included when it changes applicability. This rule prevents a mechanically correct quotation from acquiring a broader meaning during summarization. The failure family of mapping a near-synonym to a semantically adjacent but wrong concept illustrates why this additional context is necessary. We do not treat quotation matching as sufficient proof of scientific support. It establishes that words appeared in the source, whereas the question of whether those words support the whole claim requires a separate contextual judgment.

observations.quote: A numerical contrast can be compatible with several mechanisms. In ArchiveQA-Sim, qualitative traces suggest that entity-aware query expansion changes which museum object record is selected and how its qualifications survive evidence assembly. This pattern is consistent with the intended intervention, but the interpretation remains bounded by the randomized query-level controlled experiment. The assigned comparison concerns the specified software component, and extrapolation to other mechanisms or practical outcomes would exceed what was assigned. A plausible narrative does not repair a design limitation. We therefore separate the reported score change from a broader claim that the intervention is the sole cause of a practical improvement. The result also does not imply that single-pass dense retrieval is universally inferior: the reference pipeline may behave differently under another corpus composition, update schedule, or evidence budget. Those counterfactual settings were not measured here.

observations.quote: Resource accounting is reported separately from Recall@5. The fictional baseline monetary cost was USD 0.021 per query, and intervention cost was USD 0.031 per query.
